rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track;

SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS AlbumCount FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(al.AlbumId) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM Album GROUP BY ArtistId))
rows.note: Assuming "most albums" means the most rows in the Album table linked to an artist, with ties included.

rows.sql: SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer GROUP BY Country ORDER BY Country;
rows.note: Assuming "country" refers to the Customer table's Country column, with customers that have no country shown as NULL.

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS Year, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS TotalRevenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assuming total revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total grouped by calendar year of InvoiceDate.

rows.sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS TotalSpent FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assumption: total spent is the sum of Invoice.Total per customer, and full name is FirstName plus LastName.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS CustomerCount FROM Employee e JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assuming "looks after" means Customer.SupportRepId, I'll count customers per employee and return the top one(s) by full name.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM PlaylistTrack pt JOIN Playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = pt.PlaylistId WHERE p.Name = 'Grunge';
SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_purchased_tracks FROM Track t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM InvoiceLine il WHERE il.TrackId = t.TrackId);
rows.note: I'm counting tracks that have no row in InvoiceLine, since that table records every sale.

rows.sql: SELECT BillingCountry, SUM(Total) AS Revenue FROM Invoice WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2012-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2013-01-01' GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: I'll sum invoice totals by BillingCountry for 2012 and return the top country.

rows.sql:
SELECT ar.Name
FROM Artist ar
JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
WHERE t.GenreId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 3;
rows.note: Assumption: a track's artist is reached via Track → Album → Artist, and genres are counted by distinct GenreId per artist.

rows.sql:
SELECT g.Name AS Genre,
ROUND(100.0 * SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) / (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) FROM InvoiceLine), 2) AS Percentage
FROM InvoiceLine il
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
GROUP BY g.Name
ORDER BY Percentage DESC
rows.note: I'll compute revenue per genre from invoice lines (UnitPrice × Quantity) as a share of the overall total.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) AS customer_count
FROM Invoice i
JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
AND i.CustomerId NOT IN (
  SELECT i2.CustomerId
  FROM Invoice i2
  JOIN InvoiceLine il2 ON il2.InvoiceId = i2.InvoiceId
  JOIN Track t2 ON t2.TrackId = il2.TrackId
  JOIN Genre g2 ON g2.GenreId = t2.GenreId
  WHERE g2.Name = 'Jazz'
);
rows.note: Assumption: a customer "bought" a track if it appears in an InvoiceLine linked to one of their invoices, and genres are matched by Genre.Name.

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS revenue FROM Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011' GROUP BY month ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total for invoices dated in 2011, grouped by calendar month.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employee e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customer c WHERE c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId)

SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_first_purchase_2010 FROM (SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_date FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) WHERE first_date >= '2010-01-01' AND first_date < '2011-01-01'
rows.note: Assumption: a customer's first purchase is their earliest invoice date, and I count customers whose earliest invoice falls in 2010.

rows.sql: SELECT Album.Title, ROUND(SUM(Track.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 1) AS TotalMinutes FROM Track JOIN Album ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId GROUP BY Album.AlbumId, Album.Title ORDER BY SUM(Track.Milliseconds) DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assumption: total running time is the sum of Track.Milliseconds per album, converted to minutes (ms / 60000).

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS Year,
         SUM(Total) AS Revenue
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY Year
),
withprev AS (
  SELECT Year, Revenue, LAG(Revenue) OVER (ORDER BY Year) AS PrevRevenue
  FROM yearly
)
SELECT Year,
       ROUND(Revenue, 2) AS Revenue,
       ROUND((Revenue - PrevRevenue) * 100.0 / PrevRevenue, 1) AS YoY_Pct_Change
FROM withprev
WHERE PrevRevenue IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue is the sum of `Invoice.Total` per calendar year, and the change is measured against the prior year.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_above_average FROM (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS spent FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) WHERE spent > (SELECT AVG(s) FROM (SELECT SUM(Total) AS s FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId));
rows.note: I'll treat each customer's total spend as the sum of their invoice Totals, and compare each against the average of those per-customer totals.

rows.sql:
WITH cnt AS (
  SELECT pt.PlaylistId, COUNT(DISTINCT al.ArtistId) AS n
  FROM PlaylistTrack pt
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  GROUP BY pt.PlaylistId
)
SELECT p.Name, c.n AS DistinctArtists
FROM cnt c
JOIN Playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = c.PlaylistId
WHERE c.n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM cnt);
rows.note: Assumption: "largest number of distinct artists" counts distinct Artist rows reached via Track → Album → Artist; ties are all returned.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 1) AS x;
rows.note: Assuming "contain tracks from more than one genre" means an invoice whose line items reference tracks with at least two distinct GenreIds.

rows.sql:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS SupportRep, SUM(i.Total) AS Revenue2010
FROM Invoice i
JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
WHERE strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2010'
GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName
HAVING SUM(i.Total) = (
  SELECT MAX(s) FROM (
    SELECT SUM(i2.Total) AS s
    FROM Invoice i2
    JOIN Customer c2 ON c2.CustomerId = i2.CustomerId
    WHERE strftime('%Y', i2.InvoiceDate) = '2010' AND c2.SupportRepId IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY c2.SupportRepId
  )
);
rows.note: I'm assuming "revenue" means the sum of `Invoice.Total` for invoices dated in 2010, attributed to each customer's support rep. Returning only the top rep (ties included).

rows.sql:
WITH r AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) AS Year, g.Name AS Genre, SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS Revenue
  FROM InvoiceLine il
  JOIN Invoice i ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
  JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
  JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
  GROUP BY 1, 2
), k AS (
  SELECT Year, Genre, Revenue, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Year ORDER BY Revenue DESC) AS rk FROM r
)
SELECT Year, Genre FROM k WHERE rk = 2 ORDER BY Year;

WITH s AS (
  SELECT CustomerId,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2013' THEN Total ELSE 0 END) AS t2013,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2012' THEN Total ELSE 0 END) AS t2012
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY CustomerId
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_spent_more_in_2013_than_2012
FROM s
WHERE t2013 > t2012;
rows.note: Assumption: spending is the sum of `Invoice.Total` per customer for each calendar year, and a customer with no invoices in a year counts as 0 for that year.

rows.sql: SELECT AVG(Total) AS median_total FROM (SELECT Total FROM Invoice ORDER BY Total LIMIT 2 - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Invoice) % 2 OFFSET ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Invoice) - 1) / 2)
rows.note: Assuming the median is taken over all rows in the Invoice table's Total column (averaging the two middle values when the count is even).

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(DISTINCT pt.PlaylistId) AS PlaylistCount
  FROM Artist ar
  JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
  JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
  JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.TrackId = t.TrackId
  GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
)
SELECT ArtistId, Name, PlaylistCount
FROM counts
WHERE PlaylistCount = (SELECT MAX(PlaylistCount) FROM counts);
rows.note: I'm assuming "appear in" means a track by the artist (via its album) is in the playlist, and I'll return all artists tied for the top count.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(1.0 * COUNT(*) / COUNT(DISTINCT InvoiceId), 2) AS avg_line_items_per_invoice FROM InvoiceLine;
rows.note: Assuming line items are rows in InvoiceLine and the average is taken over all invoices (including any with zero lines is unlikely, so I'll compute over invoices that have lines).

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS discontinued_products FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '1';
rows.note: I'm assuming discontinued products are those with Discontinued = '1'.

rows.sql: SELECT CompanyName FROM Suppliers WHERE Country = 'Germany';
rows.note: I'm assuming "based in Germany" means the Country column equals 'Germany'.

rows.sql: SELECT c.CategoryName, COUNT(p.ProductID) AS ProductCount FROM Categories c JOIN Products p ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName ORDER BY ProductCount DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS Year, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assuming "placed" means OrderDate, grouped by calendar year.

rows.sql: SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName, ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS AvgFreight FROM Orders o JOIN Shippers s ON o.ShipVia = s.ShipperID GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY s.CompanyName;
rows.note: Assuming "shipper" means the ShipVia shipper on each order, and I'll average Orders.Freight per shipper.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employees e WHERE e.ReportsTo = (SELECT EmployeeID FROM Employees WHERE FirstName = 'Andrew' AND LastName = 'Fuller');

WITH counts AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2020'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, FullName
)
SELECT FullName, OrderCount
FROM counts
WHERE OrderCount = (SELECT MAX(OrderCount) FROM counts);
rows.note: Assuming "in 2020" means OrderDate falls within calendar year 2020, and ties are all returned.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_products FROM Products WHERE UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM Products);
rows.note: Assuming "average product unit price" means the simple average of Products.UnitPrice across all products.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders WHERE ShipCountry = 'France';
rows.note: Assuming "shipped to France" means ShipCountry = 'France' in the Orders table, counting all rows regardless of ShippedDate.

rows.sql: SELECT p.ProductName, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS Revenue FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName ORDER BY SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assumption: revenue per line = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount), summed per product, with the top 5 by that total.

rows.sql: SELECT c.CategoryName, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID WHERE p.UnitPrice = (SELECT MAX(p2.UnitPrice) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID) ORDER BY c.CategoryName;
rows.note: Assumption: "most expensive" means the highest `Products.UnitPrice` within each category, and ties are all shown.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT o.CustomerID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021'
  GROUP BY o.CustomerID
)
SELECT c.CompanyName, r.revenue
FROM rev r
JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = r.CustomerID
WHERE r.revenue = (SELECT MAX(revenue) FROM rev);
rows.note: Assuming revenue is the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over order lines, with orders counted by OrderDate in 2021.

rows.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, order_count FROM m WHERE order_count = (SELECT MAX(order_count) FROM m);
rows.note: I'll count orders by calendar month for 2021 based on OrderDate, returning every month tied for the highest count.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '1997'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName
)
SELECT EmployeeID, FirstName, LastName, OrderCount
FROM counts
WHERE OrderCount = (SELECT MAX(OrderCount) FROM counts);
rows.note: The Orders table has no orders from 1997. OrderDate ranges from 2012-07-10 to 2023-10-28, so no employee can be credited with 1997 orders.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_shipped_orders FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL AND ShippedDate > RequiredDate;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped after their required date" means ShippedDate is not NULL and ShippedDate > RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(ShippedDate) - julianday(OrderDate)), 1) AS avg_days_to_ship FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and the average is over the difference in days between ShippedDate and OrderDate.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '0' AND UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel;
rows.note: Assuming "still sold" means Discontinued = '0' and "below reorder level" means UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel.

rows.sql: SELECT c.Country, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2019' GROUP BY c.Country ORDER BY OrderCount DESC LIMIT 1;

SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.CategoryName = 'Beverages' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) / SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 1) AS beverages_pct FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2023';
rows.note: I'm treating revenue as UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from Order Details, filtered to orders dated in 2023.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_with_orders_every_month_2020
FROM (
  SELECT CustomerID
  FROM Orders
  WHERE OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2021-01-01'
  GROUP BY CustomerID
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%m', OrderDate)) = 12
) t;
rows.note: I'm assuming OrderDate is stored as ISO text and counting distinct calendar months of 2020 per customer.

rows.sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS order_value
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID
),
emp_avg AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID, AVG(order_value) AS avg_order_value
  FROM order_totals
  GROUP BY EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, ea.avg_order_value
FROM emp_avg ea
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = ea.EmployeeID
WHERE ea.avg_order_value = (SELECT MAX(avg_order_value) FROM emp_avg)

WITH rev AS (
  SELECT s.CompanyName AS SupplierName,
         SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS Revenue
  FROM "Order Details" od
  JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
  JOIN Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018'
  GROUP BY s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName
)
SELECT SupplierName, Revenue
FROM rev
WHERE Revenue = (SELECT MAX(Revenue) FROM rev);
rows.note: I'll treat revenue as UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from Order Details, filtered to orders dated in 2018, grouped by supplier, and return only the top supplier (all tied rows if there's a tie).

rows.sql:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT od.ProductID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units2021,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2022' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units2022
  FROM "Order Details" od
  JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  GROUP BY od.ProductID
)
SELECT p.ProductName, s.units2021, s.units2022, (s.units2022 - s.units2021) AS increase
FROM s
JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = s.ProductID
WHERE (s.units2022 - s.units2021) = (SELECT MAX(units2022 - units2021) FROM s);
rows.note: I'm assuming "units sold" means the sum of `Quantity` in Order Details, grouped by the calendar year of `Orders.OrderDate`, and that ties for the largest increase should all be shown.

rows.sql:
SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN o.ShippedDate > o.RequiredDate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS LatePercentage
FROM Orders o
JOIN Shippers s ON s.ShipperID = o.ShipVia
WHERE o.ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName
ORDER BY s.CompanyName;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and "arrived after the required date" means ShippedDate > RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT yr AS Year, cnt AS OrdersInYear, SUM(cnt) OVER (ORDER BY yr ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS CumulativeOrders FROM (SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Orders GROUP BY yr) ORDER BY yr
rows.note: I'll count orders per year from OrderDate and accumulate them in year order.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_over_10000
FROM (
  SELECT OrderID, SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) AS total
  FROM "Order Details"
  GROUP BY OrderID
  HAVING total > 10000
) t;
rows.note: Assuming total value = sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) per order, counting orders where that sum exceeds 10,000.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT o.EmployeeID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) AS rev2018,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2019' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) AS rev2019
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName,
       ROUND(r.rev2018, 2) AS Revenue2018,
       ROUND(r.rev2019, 2) AS Revenue2019,
       ROUND(r.rev2019 - r.rev2018, 2) AS Increase
FROM rev r
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = r.EmployeeID
ORDER BY Increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'll compute each employee's after-discount revenue (UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount)) for 2018 and 2019 by order date, then return the employee with the largest increase.
